ASSURED SHORTHOLD TENANCY AGREEMENT
for a furnished flat

This Agreement is made on the date set out in the Particulars below. It creates an assured shorthold tenancy as defined in section 19A of the Housing Act 1988 (as amended). Please read it carefully before signing. If there is anything you do not understand, you should take independent advice before you sign. This Agreement is legally binding.

Agent reference: LH/LT27-3/2025-11
Prepared by Lindqvist & Hart Lettings, 4 Corn Exchange Passage (“the Agent”)

========================================================
PART A — PARTICULARS
========================================================

A1. Date of this Agreement: 14 November 2025

A2. Landlord: Harriet Penrose-Vale, c/o Lindqvist & Hart Lettings, 4 Corn Exchange Passage. Address for service of notices (including notices under sections 47 and 48 of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1987): as above.

A3. Tenants: Callum Ostrowski and Neha Batra (each a “Tenant” and together “the Tenant”).

A4. Property: Flat 3, 27 Linden Terrace, including the fixtures, fittings and furniture listed in the Inventory (Schedule 3), together with the right to use the Common Parts in common with the other occupiers of the Building.

A5. Building: 27 Linden Terrace, a converted Victorian house containing four self-contained flats.

A6. Term: 12 months, starting on 1 December 2025 (“the Start Date”) and ending on 30 November 2026 (“the End Date”), subject to clause 18 (Break Clause).

A7. Rent: £1,375 (one thousand three hundred and seventy-five pounds) per calendar month, payable in advance on the 1st day of each month. The first payment is due on or before the Start Date.

A8. Deposit: £1,586, being five weeks' Rent, to be protected with the Tenancy Deposit Protection scheme named in Schedule 1.

A9. Permitted Occupiers: the Tenants only. No other person may live at the Property without the Landlord's written consent.

A10. Bank details for Rent: provided separately by the Agent in writing. The Agent will never change bank details by email alone. If you receive an email asking you to pay Rent to a new account, telephone the Agent on 555-0161 before paying anything.

========================================================
PART B — TERMS AND CONDITIONS
========================================================

1. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

1.1 In this Agreement, unless the context requires otherwise:
(a) “Building” means the building described in A5, including its roof, foundations, external walls, Common Parts and grounds.
(b) “Common Parts” means the entrance hall, stairs, landings, the bin store, the rear garden path and the bicycle store, and any other part of the Building that the Landlord makes available for use by the occupiers in common.
(c) “Inventory” means the schedule of condition and contents in Schedule 3, together with the photographic check-in report dated on or around the Start Date, which the Tenant will be given a copy of and invited to comment on within 7 days.
(d) “Utilities” means gas, electricity, water and sewerage, telephone, broadband and any television or streaming subscriptions.
(e) “Working Day” means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or bank holiday in England.

1.2 Where there is more than one Tenant, the obligations of the Tenant are joint and several (see clause 23).

1.3 Any obligation on the Tenant not to do something includes an obligation not to allow anyone else to do it, including visitors.

1.4 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this Agreement.

1.5 References to the Landlord include the Agent where the Agent is acting on the Landlord's behalf, and include anyone who becomes entitled to the Landlord's interest in the Property.

2. GRANT AND RENT

2.1 The Landlord lets the Property to the Tenant for the Term at the Rent.

2.2 The Tenant will pay the Rent on the dates in A7 by standing order to the account notified by the Agent. Rent is not considered paid until it reaches that account in cleared funds.

2.3 If any Rent remains unpaid 14 days after the date it was due, the Tenant will pay interest on it at 3% per year above the Bank of England base rate from the date it was due until the date it is paid. No other fee or charge is payable for late payment.

2.4 The Rent will not be increased during the Term. If the tenancy continues after the End Date as a periodic tenancy, the Landlord may propose a new Rent by giving notice under section 13 of the Housing Act 1988, and the Tenant may refer that proposal to the First-tier Tribunal if they disagree with it.

2.5 The Rent includes the Landlord's buildings insurance and the service charge for the Building. It does not include Utilities or Council Tax.

3. DEPOSIT

3.1 The Tenant will pay the Deposit to the Agent on or before the date of this Agreement. The Deposit will be protected in the scheme named in Schedule 1 within 30 days of receipt, and the prescribed information in Schedule 1 is given to the Tenant with this Agreement.

3.2 The Deposit is held as security for the performance of the Tenant's obligations and may be applied, at the end of the tenancy, towards:
(a) any Rent or other money lawfully due under this Agreement that remains unpaid;
(b) the reasonable cost of repairing damage to the Property or its contents, or of replacing items missing from the Inventory, beyond fair wear and tear;
(c) the reasonable cost of cleaning the Property to the standard recorded at check-in, where it is not returned in that standard;
(d) any Utilities or Council Tax that the Landlord becomes liable to pay because the Tenant did not pay it;
(e) the reasonable cost of replacing lost keys or fobs, or changing locks where keys are not returned.

3.3 The Deposit may not be used by the Tenant as payment of the last month's Rent.

3.4 The Landlord will propose any deductions in writing within 10 Working Days of the end of the tenancy, with reasons and evidence. Any part of the Deposit that is not in dispute will be returned within 10 days of the parties agreeing the amount. If the parties cannot agree, either may refer the dispute to the scheme's free alternative dispute resolution service.

3.5 “Fair wear and tear” means the deterioration that happens through ordinary, reasonable use of the Property and its contents over time, taking into account the length of the tenancy, the number of occupiers and the age and quality of each item at the Start Date.

4. UTILITIES AND COUNCIL TAX

4.1 From the Start Date the Tenant is responsible for paying for all Utilities supplied to the Property and for the Council Tax, and will notify the suppliers and the local authority of the start of the tenancy, giving meter readings as recorded on the Inventory.

4.2 The Tenant may change the supplier of any Utility, but must tell the Agent which supplier they have chosen and must not change the type of supply, meter or tariff in a way that requires physical alterations to the Property (for example, installing a prepayment meter) without the Landlord's written consent.

4.3 The Tenant will not allow any Utility to be disconnected for non-payment.

4.4 At the end of the tenancy the Tenant will provide final meter readings to the suppliers and the Agent and will pay all final bills.

4.5 Water is supplied through a meter in the pavement outside the Building which serves Flat 3 only. The water company's account reference is given on the Inventory.

5. USE OF THE PROPERTY

5.1 The Tenant will use the Property as a private home for the Permitted Occupiers only.

5.2 The Tenant will not carry on any trade, business or profession at the Property, except that the Tenant may work from home in a way that does not involve visits by clients or customers, deliveries beyond ordinary household levels, the storage of stock or equipment, or any change to the residential character of the Property.

5.3 The Tenant will not use the Property for any illegal or immoral purpose.

5.4 The Tenant will not take in lodgers or paying guests, or advertise the Property or any part of it on any short-term letting platform.

5.5 The Tenant may have overnight guests occasionally, provided that no guest stays for more than 14 nights in any period of three months without the Landlord's written consent.

5.6 The Tenant will not leave the Property unoccupied for more than 21 consecutive days without telling the Agent in writing beforehand, and during any such absence will take reasonable steps to secure the Property and prevent frozen pipes (for example, by leaving the heating on a low setting during the winter months).

6. CONDITION AND REPAIRS

6.1 Landlord's repairing obligations. The Landlord will keep in repair the structure and exterior of the Property and the Building (including drains, gutters and external pipes), and will keep in repair and proper working order the installations for the supply of water, gas, electricity, sanitation, space heating and water heating, as required by section 11 of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985. The Landlord will also keep the Common Parts in repair and reasonably clean and lit.

6.2 The Landlord will keep the furniture, appliances and other items listed in the Inventory in working order, and will repair or replace any that break through fair wear and tear or no fault of the Tenant.

6.3 Tenant's obligations. The Tenant will:
(a) keep the interior of the Property clean and in the condition recorded in the Inventory, fair wear and tear excepted;
(b) use the Property in a tenant-like manner, which includes doing the small jobs a reasonable occupier would do, such as replacing light bulbs and smoke-alarm batteries, unblocking sinks and toilets blocked by the Tenant's own use, bleeding radiators, and keeping drains and gullies free of the Tenant's waste;
(c) report to the Agent promptly, and in writing where possible, any disrepair or defect in the Property or the Building of which the Tenant becomes aware, including leaks, damp, mould, faulty appliances, and problems with the heating or hot water;
(d) not cause or allow any damage to the Property or the Building, and pay the reasonable cost of repairing any damage caused by the Tenant or their visitors, other than fair wear and tear;
(e) ventilate the Property adequately, including using extractor fans when cooking and bathing, opening windows regularly, and not drying laundry on radiators without ventilating the room, so as to reduce condensation;
(f) keep the gutters' downpipes at ground level and the rear yard gully clear of leaves where they are accessible from the Property's own outside space.

6.4 Damp and mould. The Landlord recognises that damp and mould can be caused by structural defects as well as by how a home is lived in. If the Tenant reports damp or mould, the Landlord will arrange an inspection within 14 days and will carry out any works needed to deal with the cause within a reasonable time. Nothing in this clause makes the Tenant responsible for damp or mould caused by disrepair, by a defect in the structure, or by the Landlord's failure to provide adequate heating or ventilation.

6.5 Emergencies. In an emergency (for example, a major water leak, no heating or hot water in winter, a smell of gas, or a security problem with the front door), the Tenant should call the Agent's out-of-hours line on 555-0162, or for a gas leak, the national gas emergency number first. Where the Tenant cannot reach the Agent and the matter cannot wait, the Tenant may arrange for a qualified contractor to carry out the minimum works needed to make the Property safe, and the Landlord will reimburse the reasonable cost on production of a receipt.

7. LANDLORD'S ACCESS

7.1 The Tenant will allow the Landlord, the Agent and their contractors to enter the Property at reasonable times of day to inspect its condition, carry out repairs or safety checks, or (in the last two months of the Term) to show the Property to prospective tenants or buyers.

7.2 Except in an emergency, the Landlord will give at least 24 hours' written notice before any visit, stating the reason, and will try to agree a convenient time with the Tenant. The Tenant may ask to be present.

7.3 Routine inspections will take place no more than once every three months.

7.4 In a genuine emergency that threatens the safety of people or the fabric of the Building, the Landlord may enter without notice, but will tell the Tenant as soon as possible afterwards and leave the Property secure.

8. ALTERATIONS AND DECORATION

8.1 The Tenant will not make any alterations or additions to the Property, including changing the locks, installing satellite dishes or external aerials, or removing any of the Landlord's fixtures, without the Landlord's prior written consent.

8.2 The Tenant will not redecorate the Property without the Landlord's prior written consent. The Landlord will not unreasonably refuse a request to repaint walls in a neutral colour, provided that the work is done to a professional standard. The Tenant may hang pictures using small picture hooks or removable adhesive strips. Small holes left by picture hooks will be treated as fair wear and tear.

8.3 The Tenant may not attach anything to the external walls or windows of the Property, including window boxes, without consent, because the Building is in a conservation area.

8.4 The Tenant may install, at their own cost, a broadband connection from any provider, provided that any new cabling inside the Property is run neatly along skirting boards and any work to the external wall or Common Parts is done by the provider's engineers with the Agent's prior agreement.

9. NUISANCE, NOISE AND NEIGHBOURS

9.1 The Tenant will not do anything at the Property or in the Building which causes a nuisance or annoyance to the other occupiers of the Building or to neighbours, or which might invalidate the Landlord's insurance.

9.2 The Tenant will not play music, televisions or instruments loudly enough to be heard outside the Property between 11 pm and 8 am.

9.3 The Property has wooden floors. The Tenant will use the rugs supplied with the Inventory in the living room and bedroom, and will not remove them for the duration of the tenancy, to reduce noise transmission to Flat 1 below.

9.4 The Tenant will not use the Common Parts for storage, and will not leave shoes, buggies, parcels, furniture or rubbish on the stairs or landings, which must be kept clear as a fire escape route.

10. ASSIGNMENT AND SUBLETTING

10.1 The Tenant will not assign, sublet, part with or share possession of the whole or any part of the Property.

10.2 If one Tenant wishes to leave and a replacement tenant is proposed, the Landlord will consider the request reasonably. Any replacement will be subject to the Agent's usual referencing, and a new agreement or deed of variation will be needed. The Agent's charge for this is limited to £50 including VAT, as permitted by law.

11. SMOKING, PETS AND OTHER RESTRICTIONS

11.1 The Tenant will not smoke tobacco or any other substance, or use e-cigarettes or vaping devices, inside the Property or in the Common Parts. Smoking is permitted in the rear garden only, away from open windows.

11.2 The Tenant will not keep any oil heaters, paraffin heaters or bottled-gas appliances at the Property.

11.3 The Tenant will not keep any barbecue on the Property's balcony, and will not use any barbecue in the rear garden within three metres of the Building.

11.4 Animals. The Tenant may keep one cat at the Property, or one small caged animal (for example a hamster, rabbit or guinea pig), but only with the Landlord's prior written consent. A request for consent must be made in writing, and the Landlord will not unreasonably refuse or delay it; the Landlord will give a decision within 28 days. Consent may be given subject to reasonable conditions, such as the Tenant arranging insurance that covers damage caused by the animal. Dogs are not permitted at the Property because the lease of the Building, under which the Landlord holds the flat, prohibits them; this restriction does not apply to an assistance dog. Fish in a tank of up to 60 litres do not need consent.

11.5 If an animal is kept, the Tenant will be responsible for keeping it under control, preventing it from causing a nuisance, and for the cost of professional cleaning and flea treatment of the Property at the end of the tenancy where reasonably necessary.

12. INSURANCE

12.1 The Landlord will insure the Building and the Landlord's contents against the usual risks. The Landlord's insurance does not cover the Tenant's own belongings, and the Tenant is advised to take out their own contents insurance.

12.2 The Tenant will not do anything that might make the Landlord's insurance void or increase the premium, and will tell the Agent promptly of any damage to the Property that might give rise to an insurance claim.

12.3 If the Property is made uninhabitable by fire, flood or another insured risk not caused by the Tenant, the Rent (or a fair proportion of it) will stop being payable until the Property is fit to live in again. Either party may then end this Agreement by giving one month's written notice if the Property has not been reinstated within six months.

13. KEYS, LOCKS AND SECURITY

13.1 At the start of the tenancy, the Tenant will be given the keys and fobs listed in Part C of Schedule 3. The Tenant will sign the Inventory to confirm receipt.

13.2 The Tenant will not have additional keys cut, or additional fobs programmed, without the Agent's consent, which will not be unreasonably refused. Any extra keys must be handed over at the end of the tenancy.

13.3 The Tenant will lock the doors and windows of the Property whenever it is left empty, and will make sure the main front door of the Building closes behind them.

13.4 If the Tenant loses a key or fob, they will tell the Agent promptly. The Tenant will pay the reasonable cost of replacing it and, if security is compromised (for example, if the key was lost with something showing the address), of changing the relevant lock.

13.5 If the Tenant is locked out, the Agent will try to help during office hours, but cannot guarantee to attend out of hours. The cost of a locksmith called by the Tenant is the Tenant's responsibility.

14. GAS, ELECTRICAL AND APPLIANCE SAFETY

14.1 The Landlord will ensure that every gas appliance and flue at the Property is checked for safety by a Gas Safe registered engineer at least once every 12 months, and will give the Tenant a copy of the current gas safety record before the Start Date and within 28 days of each new check.

14.2 The Landlord will ensure that the electrical installation at the Property is inspected and tested by a qualified person at least every five years, and will give the Tenant a copy of the current report.

14.3 The Tenant will allow access for these checks on reasonable notice under clause 7.

14.4 The Tenant will not tamper with any gas or electrical installation, and will not use any portable appliance that the Tenant knows or suspects is unsafe.

15. FIRE SAFETY

15.1 The Property has a smoke alarm in the hallway, a heat alarm in the kitchen and a carbon monoxide alarm next to the boiler. The Landlord will check that these are working on the Start Date.

15.2 The Tenant will test the alarms at least once a month, replace batteries where needed, and report any fault to the Agent immediately. The Tenant will not disconnect or cover any alarm.

15.3 The flat entrance door is a fire door. The Tenant will not prop it open, remove its self-closing device, or fit anything (including a cat flap) that affects its fire resistance.

15.4 A fire blanket is fixed in the kitchen. The Tenant should familiarise themselves with the fire action notice in the entrance hall of the Building.

16. REFUSE AND RECYCLING

16.1 The Tenant will put household waste and recycling in the communal bins in the bin store at the front of the Building, sorted as instructed by the local authority, and will not leave bags beside the bins.

16.2 Collection days are posted in the bin store. Bins must be put out on the pavement by whichever occupier's turn it is on the rota (see Schedule 2) and brought back in the same day.

16.3 Bulky items (furniture, mattresses, appliances) must be disposed of through the local authority's bulky waste service or a licensed waste carrier, at the Tenant's cost, and must not be left in the Common Parts or on the street.

17. BICYCLES, GARDEN AND COMMON PARTS

17.1 The Tenant may keep up to two bicycles in the communal bicycle store at the side of the Building, which is opened with a fob. The bicycle store is shared with the other flats and is not covered by the Landlord's insurance; bicycles must be locked to the stands provided.

17.2 Bicycles may not be kept in the Common Parts or carried up the stairs, except for folding bicycles, which may be kept inside the Property.

17.3 The rear garden is shared by all four flats. The Tenant may use it for quiet recreation and for drying laundry on the rotary line. The Landlord arranges for the lawn to be cut and the hedges trimmed; the Tenant is not responsible for gardening.

17.4 Flat 3 has the use of a small private balcony off the kitchen. The Tenant will keep it clean and free of standing water, and will not place anything heavy on it (including large plant pots or hot tubs). The balcony is not to be used for storage.

18. BREAK CLAUSE

18.1 Either the Landlord or the Tenant may end this tenancy early by giving the other at least two months' notice in writing, provided that the notice does not expire before the last day of the sixth month of the Term (that is, 31 May 2026).

18.2 Notice given by the Tenant must be signed by all Tenants, or by one Tenant with the written agreement of the others.

18.3 Notice given by the Landlord under this clause must be given in the form and manner required by law (currently a notice under section 21 of the Housing Act 1988 or any provision that replaces it) and does not on its own entitle the Landlord to recover possession without a court order.

18.4 The Tenant must pay Rent up to the date on which the notice expires, and any Rent paid in advance for a period after that date will be refunded.

19. AT THE END OF THE TENANCY

19.1 At the end of the tenancy the Tenant will:
(a) give vacant possession of the Property, removing all their belongings and rubbish;
(b) leave the Property and the Inventory items clean and in the condition recorded at the start, fair wear and tear excepted, with the furniture in the rooms it was in at the Start Date;
(c) return all keys and fobs listed in Part C of Schedule 3, together with any extra keys cut during the tenancy, to the Agent's office by 12 noon on the last day;
(d) give the Agent a forwarding address in writing;
(e) take final meter readings and give them to the suppliers and the Agent.

19.2 The Agent will carry out a check-out inspection against the Inventory, which the Tenant is invited to attend.

19.3 Professional cleaning will not be required as a condition of the tenancy. The Tenant need only return the Property to the standard of cleanliness recorded at check-in. If the Property is not returned to that standard, the reasonable cost of bringing it up to that standard may be deducted under clause 3.2(c).

19.4 Any belongings left in the Property after the Tenant has left will be stored for 14 days, during which the Agent will write to the Tenant at their forwarding address. After 14 days the Landlord may dispose of them, and may deduct the reasonable cost of storage and disposal from any sale proceeds or from the Deposit.

20. LANDLORD'S OBLIGATIONS

20.1 The Landlord will allow the Tenant quiet enjoyment of the Property during the tenancy without unlawful interruption by the Landlord or anyone acting for the Landlord.

20.2 The Landlord will insure the Building as set out in clause 12, and comply with the repairing, safety and deposit obligations in this Agreement and imposed by law.

20.3 The Landlord confirms that the Property is fit for human habitation at the Start Date and will keep it so throughout the tenancy, in accordance with the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 (as amended by the Homes (Fitness for Human Habitation) Act 2018).

20.4 The Landlord confirms that they have any consent required from their mortgage lender and their own landlord (under the lease of the Building) to grant this tenancy.

20.5 The Landlord will provide the Tenant with: a copy of the current Energy Performance Certificate for the Property (rating C); the current gas safety record; the current electrical installation condition report; and the Government's guide “How to rent”.

21. NOTICES AND COMMUNICATION

21.1 Any notice under this Agreement must be in writing. Notices to the Landlord may be served at the address in A2. Notices to the Tenant may be served at the Property.

21.2 The parties agree that notices (other than notices seeking possession, which must be served in accordance with the law) may also be given by email: to the Agent at lettings@lindqvist-hart.example.com and to the Tenants at the email addresses they have given the Agent. A notice sent by email is treated as received on the next Working Day after it is sent, unless the sender receives an automated message saying it was not delivered.

21.3 Day-to-day matters such as maintenance requests should be reported through the Agent's online tenant portal, which keeps a record of every report and its progress.

22. DATA PROTECTION

22.1 The Landlord and the Agent will process the Tenant's personal data in accordance with data protection law, for the purposes of managing the tenancy, protecting the Deposit, carrying out legally required checks, and dealing with any dispute.

22.2 The Tenant's details may be shared with the deposit scheme, utility suppliers, the local authority (for Council Tax), contractors who need to arrange access, and, if necessary, a court.

22.3 The Agent's privacy notice, which explains how long data is kept and the Tenant's rights, is available on request and on the Agent's website.

23. JOINT AND SEVERAL LIABILITY

23.1 Where there is more than one Tenant, each Tenant is responsible both individually and together for all of the obligations of the Tenant under this Agreement, including the payment of the whole of the Rent, not just a share of it.

23.2 This means that if one Tenant leaves or fails to pay, the Landlord may require the remaining Tenant to pay the whole Rent.

24. ENDING THE TENANCY AND POSSESSION

24.1 If the Tenant remains in occupation after the End Date and no new agreement has been signed, the tenancy will continue as a monthly periodic tenancy on the same terms (other than the Term and the Break Clause).

24.2 During a periodic tenancy the Tenant may end the tenancy by giving at least one month's written notice ending at the end of a period of the tenancy (that is, the last day of a calendar month).

24.3 The Landlord may only recover possession of the Property by obtaining a court order on one of the grounds set out in Schedule 2 to the Housing Act 1988, or by the procedure in section 21 of that Act, as each may be amended or replaced from time to time. Nothing in this Agreement allows the Landlord to recover possession without a court order.

24.4 If the law governing assured shorthold tenancies changes during the tenancy, this Agreement will take effect subject to that change.

25. GENERAL

25.1 This Agreement, together with its Schedules, is the entire agreement between the parties. No statement made before it was signed forms part of it unless it is written into it.

25.2 If any part of this Agreement is found to be unenforceable, the rest of it will continue to have effect.

25.3 Any delay by the Landlord in enforcing a term of this Agreement does not prevent the Landlord from enforcing it later.

25.4 This Agreement is governed by the law of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales have jurisdiction.

25.5 A person who is not a party to this Agreement has no right to enforce any of its terms.

========================================================
SCHEDULE 2 — HOUSE RULES FOR 27 LINDEN TERRACE
========================================================

These rules are agreed between the occupiers of all four flats and form part of each tenancy. They are meant to help everyone live together comfortably. Please keep to them.

1. Front door. Please make sure the main front door clicks shut behind you; it does not always latch on the first try, especially in cold weather. Do not wedge it open, even for deliveries.

2. Post. Each flat has its own lockable post box in the entrance hall. Parcels that do not fit may be left on the hall table for no more than 48 hours.

3. Bins. The bin rota runs in flat-number order, one week each, starting with Flat 1 in the first full week of each quarter. The rota is on the inside of the bin store door. General waste is collected on Tuesdays, recycling on alternate Fridays and food waste weekly on Fridays.

4. Stairs and landings. These are cleaned by a contractor every second Wednesday. Please keep them clear of personal items at all times (see clause 9.4).

5. Garden. The garden is shared. Please clear up after yourselves, keep noise down after 10 pm, and do not leave washing on the rotary line overnight.

6. Bicycle store. Two spaces per flat. Please don't use the store for anything other than bicycles and their accessories. Report a faulty fob to the Agent rather than leaving the store door unlocked.

7. Heating and boilers. Each flat has its own boiler. If you hear banging pipes or see water on the stairs, report it immediately — it may be coming from your flat or someone else's.

8. Building contact list. The occupiers maintain a voluntary group chat for the Building. Joining it is optional. The Agent is not a member and does not monitor it, so please report maintenance issues through the tenant portal.

9. Moving in and out. Please let the other occupiers know a few days ahead if you are moving in or out, so that they can expect furniture on the stairs. Protect the stair carpet and banisters during moves; damage to the Common Parts during a move will be charged to the occupier responsible.

10. Noise. Please be considerate. Wooden floors carry sound: use the rugs, avoid hard-soled shoes indoors late at night, and keep washing machines off between 10 pm and 7 am.

========================================================

PART A — METER READINGS ON THE START DATE (to be completed at check-in)
Electricity (meter in hall cupboard, serial ending 4471): __________ kWh

PART B — ROOM SUMMARY

Entrance hall: Laminate flooring, good condition, two minor scuffs near door. Coat hooks (4). Mirror (oval, 60 cm). Smoke alarm tested and working. Hall cupboard containing electricity meter, consumer unit and vacuum cleaner (cylinder type, working).

Living room: Wooden floorboards, sanded and varnished 2023, good condition. Rug (grey wool, 2 x 3 m) — must remain in place (clause 9.3). Two-seater sofa (green velvet, small wear on left arm). Armchair (oatmeal fabric). Coffee table (oak, ring mark on top). TV unit (white, two drawers). Floor lamp. Curtains (linen, cream) and blackout blind. Bookshelf (five shelves). Radiator with thermostatic valve. Two double sockets and one TV/aerial point. Sash windows (2), recently overhauled, working with window locks.

Kitchen: Vinyl flooring, good condition. Fitted units (cream shaker style), worktops (laminate, oak effect), one small burn mark near hob. Gas hob (four rings), electric oven, extractor hood with filter, fridge-freezer (integrated, 2022), washer-dryer (2021), dishwasher (slimline, 2022). Microwave. Kettle and toaster. Fire blanket fixed to wall. Heat alarm tested and working. Boiler in tall cupboard (combination boiler, serviced September 2025) with carbon monoxide alarm alongside, tested and working. Door to balcony (glazed, lockable).
